chunks: Ahmad b. Ali b. Ibrahim (rh) narrated to us. He said: My father narrated to us from his father Ibrahim b. Hashim from Abdullah b. al-Mughira from Amr al-Shami from al-Sadiq Ja'far b. Muhammad (as). He said:
"Surely, the number of months with Allah is twelve months in the Book of Allah on the day that He created the heavens and the Earth" [9:36].

The best of the months is the month of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, and it is the month of Ramadan. The heart of the month of Ramadan is the Night of Power. The Quran was revealed in the first night of the month of Ramadan, so welcome the month with the Quran.

key_terms.البيت المعمور: The Frequented House — the celestial counterpart of the Ka'ba in the heavens
key_terms.شهر الله: The month of Allah — an honorific designation indicating Ramadan's unique divine status among the months
key_terms.غرة الشهور: The best, foremost, or brightest of the months — using the metaphor of a blaze on a horse's forehead
key_terms.قلب شهر رمضان: The heart of Ramadan — its spiritual essence and most significant part
key_terms.ليلة القدر: The Night of Power or Decree — the holiest night in Islam, in which the Quran was first revealed

ai.seo_question: What does Imam al-Sadiq say about the virtue of the month of Ramadan and the Night of Power?
ai.summary: Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq quotes Quran 9:36 about the twelve divinely ordained months and then identifies Ramadan as the supreme month, calling it 'the month of Allah.' He further identifies the Night of Power (Laylat al-Qadr) as its spiritual core and states that the Quran descended on the first night of Ramadan. This hadith was likely narrated during the month of Ramadan itself (the assembly was held on the 8th of Ramadan, 367 AH), making it a timely exhortation to welcome the month with Quranic recitation.
word_analysis: may He have mercy on him
